questions.q: What is SQL Server Developer Edition?
options: A free, full-featured (not crippled) edition of SQL Server intended for learning and development
A time-limited trial that stops working after 30 days
A cloud-only version of SQL Server with no local install option
A paid edition discounted for students only
questions.explain: Developer Edition is genuinely free and full-featured, meant exactly for this kind of practice, not a crippled trial.

options: Oracle's free Express Edition for local practice, with resource limits but a real Oracle engine
A simulator that mimics Oracle syntax without running a real database
Oracle's name for its cloud-only free tier, with no local install available
A paid Oracle edition with a free trial period only
questions.explain: Oracle Database XE is a genuinely free, locally installable edition of real Oracle Database, just with some size/resource limits.

questions.q: Which platform in this lesson has no 'crippled' free-tier distinction at all — the free version IS the production engine?
options: MySQL Community Edition
Oracle Database XE
Snowflake's free trial
SQL Server Developer Edition
questions.explain: MySQL Community Edition is the same engine used in production everywhere, with no separate crippled free tier.

questions.q: Why does this lesson recommend starting Snowflake's and Databricks's free options later, closer to Chapter 9, rather than immediately?
options: Snowflake's free trial is time-limited, so starting it early wastes clock time before you reach the warehouse-specific lessons
Snowflake and Databricks cannot be used for free under any circumstances
They require the other four platforms to be installed first as a technical dependency
They are not real SQL platforms and are only used for a brief demo
questions.explain: Snowflake's free trial runs on a clock, so it's better to start it once you're actually working through the warehouse chapter.

questions.q: What does PostgreSQL's free offering consist of?
options: PostgreSQL itself is entirely free and open-source, with no edition split to consider
A 30-day trial identical to Snowflake's
A Community Edition with feature limits compared to a paid tier
A cloud-only free tier with no local installer
questions.explain: PostgreSQL has no commercial-vs-free edition split at all — it's simply free and open-source.
